stories.title: Swiss President's state visit begins today (5–7 Oct)
stories.body: Swiss Confederation President Guy Parmelin arrives today on a three-day state visit at PM Modi's invitation — his first state visit to India and his second trip this year (he attended the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi in February 2026). He is accompanied by a high-level delegation of senior officials and business leaders. Bilateral talks with PM Modi today (5 Oct) will review cooperation in trade and investment, science, technology and innovation, mobility, culture and people-to-people contact, plus regional and global issues; Parmelin also meets President Droupadi Murmu (who hosts a banquet) and EAM S. Jaishankar. On 7 October he participates in the 2nd India–EFTA Prosperity Summit. The visit marks one year of the India–EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) — EFTA comprises Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein, and TEPA targets USD 100 billion of investment into India over 15 years.

stories.title: India–Canada CEPA: 5th round opens in Ottawa today
stories.body: chief negotiators begin the fifth round of the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement talks in Ottawa, 5–9 October, aiming to conclude the pact by the end of this calendar year (the 4th round concluded in Mumbai on 18 September). The push matters because PM Modi is expected to visit Canada around December, and Canada's Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu will visit New Delhi later this month with a 300-strong business delegation; Sidhu and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal last met at the G20 Trade Ministers' meeting in Milwaukee. The two sides share a target of USD 70 billion in bilateral trade by 2030 (from over USD 30 billion today). CEPA is a free-trade-style pact: steep cuts or elimination of duties on maximum traded goods, easier movement of skilled professionals and more investment.

stories.title: RBI MPC meets from today; hike buzz ahead of the 7 Oct decision
stories.body: the six-member Monetary Policy Committee meets 5–7 October, with Governor Sanjay Malhotra announcing the decision on 7 October. A businessline poll of 12 bank chief economists found 11 expecting a 25 bps hike to 5.50% — only Bank of Baroda's Madan Sabnavis expects a hold — and a majority see a cumulative 50–75 bps tightening by end-FY27 (six economists see the repo at 6%). A PTI poll of 16 economists/bankers also found a majority expecting a hike with a hawkish tone (L&T's Sachchidanand Shukla dissents, expecting status quo). SBI Research forecasts hikes in October and December; BofA now expects a cumulative 100 bps of hikes through H1 2027. Drivers: CPI at 4.82% in August (third straight month above the 4% target), crude above $100/barrel, a ~6% weaker rupee, and a strengthening El Niño/weak October rainfall threatening Rabi output — with strong growth giving policy space for a pre-emptive move.

stories.title: GST Council set to debate a big enforcement reset on 7 Oct
stories.body: the GST Council is expected to consider removing tax officers' direct arrest power under Section 69 of the CGST Act; any arrest would instead need judicial authorisation. Other proposals in the package: raising the prosecution threshold from ₹1 crore to ₹5 crore; narrowing the scope of criminal proceedings so routine disputes over classification, valuation or ITC don't turn criminal; protecting genuine buyers' input tax credit; and easing GST registration for small e-commerce sellers. Intentional fraud would still be prosecuted (through courts, under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita), and tax recovery, interest and penalties continue. Nothing is decided yet — this is a proposal to watch — and legislative changes would need to come, potentially in the Winter Session of Parliament.

stories.title: Five Centres of Excellence for classical languages approved
stories.body: the Ministry of Education's Department of Higher Education (Language Division, OM dated 1 October 2026) approved five Centres of Excellence for studies in Classical Assamese, Classical Bengali, Classical Marathi, Classical Pali and Classical Prakrit. The host institutions: Classical Assamese — Tezpur University (Assam); Classical Bengali — Visva-Bharati University (West Bengal); Classical Marathi — Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (Deemed University), Pune (Maharashtra); Classical Pali — Central University of Odisha; Classical Prakrit — Central University of Gujarat. The CoEs will anchor advanced research, documentation, preservation and digitisation of linguistic and literary resources, and wider dissemination of the heritage of these classical languages.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi's 'Satyagraha' platform goes live
stories.body: Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi launched the 'Satyagraha' digital platform on 3 October (a day after Mahatma Gandhi's 157th birth anniversary) to bring issue-based protests across India onto a single interactive map. Citizens can register their movement and grievance in a short online form; within nine hours, over 10,000 people and groups had signed up — students, farmers, Adivasis, Dalits, OBCs, women and Gen Z — with early entries spanning education and examinations, land rights, farmers' issues, corruption, environment and health. Congress pledges to read every submission and stand with each movement in Parliament, on the streets and through letters. At the 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' event in Pune, the Maharashtra Competitive Examination Coordination Committee registered its anti-paper-leak movement as 'satyagraha', demanding the MPSC chairman's resignation, an honest and qualified officer in his place, and immediate filling of 70,000+ vacant government posts.

stories.title: Congress state chiefs meet today over EC agitation
stories.body: the Congress holds a meeting of all AICC in-charges and PCC chiefs in New Delhi today (5 Oct) to finalise its strategy for a planned agitation against the Election Commission of India over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls; the party has sought action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, while the EC has rejected the allegations. The INDIA bloc has announced a nationwide 'Save Democracy March' at district level from 2 to 8 October.

stories.title: Kautilya Conclave's final day; US carriers in focus
stories.body: the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave (theme "Resilience in an Age of Flux") concludes today in New Delhi after opening on 3 October; RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra warned that systemic risks are increasingly exogenous, cross-border and interconnected, with the next crisis potentially starting from a geopolitical event, cyberattack or tech failure. On the world front, the US has deployed its third aircraft carrier to the theatre as the conflict with Iran enters its eighth month — relevant context for India's oil-import and inflation watch, with the G7 already agreeing to release 100 million barrels from emergency reserves.
